title: Environmental factors predicting blood lead levels in pregnant women in the UK: the ALSPAC study.
ehr_evidence: The study sample was derived from the ALSPAC study, a population-based study investigating environmental and genetic influences on the health, behaviour and development of children.
summary: Observational cohort study assessing environmental, lifestyle, and socioeconomic factors associated with blood lead levels in pregnant women and their children in the UK.
key_findings: Mean maternal blood lead level was 3.67 ± 1.47 mg/dl (n=4285).
Higher educational qualification was a strong independent predictor of BLL ≥5 mg/dl (OR 1.26, 95% CI 1.12–1.42; p<0.001).
Cigarette smoking, alcohol consumption, coffee drinking, and coal fire heating were independently associated with increased BLL.
Dietary calcium intake and iron supplementation showed protective effects against high lead levels.
Maternal and child BLL at 30 months were significantly correlated (r = 0.278, n = 233; p<0.001).
population: pregnant women in the Avon area of the UK (n=4285) and their children at 30 months
exposure_domain: environmental lead exposure, lifestyle factors, diet, and socioeconomic status
limitations: selection bias (women with BLL data were older and more educated than the full cohort)
lack of data on housing age and renovation activities
child BLL samples analyzed using different methods and at different times than maternal samples
